name: Academic Classical Oil
description: A calm, still scene look with academic oil-painting brushwork, smooth blended transitions, warm low-angle light, and a deliberately incident-free composition.
style_bible: Academic and classical oil-painting technique, painted for stillness. Medium and surface: old-master technique with rich layered glazes slowly built over primed ground, smooth blended brushwork with visible impasto brushwork reserved for the brightest tactile edge, revealing fine canvas texture beneath a soft even sheen across the whole canvas; fine craquelure, painterly edges, and a warm museum varnish tone over everything. Edges and shapes: firm and carefully drawn where the light falls on stone or cloth, softening in the shadows, with reflected light carried up into every shadow so that nothing goes truly black; distance rendered by warm aerial haze rather than by loss of drawing. Palette: warm ivory, bleached marble white, honey, amber, old gold and sun-warmed rose, set against restrained sea-blue, olive, and dusty terracotta accents; low saturation, high key, and no colour permitted to shout. Lighting: broad warm directional light entering from one side at a low angle, laying long soft-edged bars of light across the surfaces; no hard-edged theatrical spotlight, no cold light, no night, no dramatic chiaroscuro. Texture: tactile impasto accents on bright surfaces, woven canvas texture showing through translucent layered glazes, polished stone, bleached plaster, sheer cloth, heavy woven fabric, aged metal with a soft patina, still reflective surfaces, and the fine grain of dust in a shaft of light. Subject grammar: one clear focal subject at rest and a deliberate absence of incident. Where the scene includes figures, they are anonymous and never recognisable individuals, are always at ease, and are shown at middle distance or further so that no face carries the frame. Framing: eye level or slightly raised, horizontals kept level and calm, generous open negative space, the subject placed off-centre and small, and the composition resolved rather than dynamic. Low stimulation is the contract: nothing is beginning or ending, no incident, no motion, no confrontation, no crowd pressing forward, no face close to camera, and no strong tonal contrast anywhere. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed place, monument, event, or copied composition.
